correctness.rationale: Construct a compact nonnegative normalized smooth bump with a plateau at 0 and nonzero mth derivative elsewhere. Its reflected dilation rho_t tends to delta in distributions; differentiation gives F=(-1)^m t^{-n-m}partial_1^m phi(-x/t), converging distributionally to partial_1^m delta. The plateau gives F(0,t)=0 and compact support gives eventually F(x,t)=0 for each fixed x!=0. The substitution y=-x/t yields exactly ∫|F|^p = C t^(n-(n+m)p), where C>0 finite. On any compact neighborhood of 0 the support lies inside for small t, proving both boundedness for p<=n/(n+m) and divergence for larger p; the endpoint is constant, not logarithmic. For any fixed 0<p<1 choosing m=1 and n>=p/(1-p) gives an obstruction. No numerical sampling is required.
